frase_gancho.texto: Vanilla, violins, and altars of flowers on the plains of the Gulf.

introduccion_narrativa.texto: You descend from the sierra toward the lowlands of the Gulf, hot, green, and full of rivers. Here live the Huastecs, who call themselves Teenek, and the Totonacs, alongside the Nahua and other peoples. It is a land of violins and jaranas, of vanilla, of coffee plantations, and of flower altars for the dead. The Teenek speak a language of the Maya family, even though they live hundreds of kilometers from the Maya; the Totonacs preserve rituals as impressive as that of the Voladores (Flyers). This hall brings together a quechquémitl, an altar for the dead, a white costume from Papantla, and a dance mask.
